On April 15, 2015, Peter Chiarelli was fired by the Boston Bruins. On May 20, the Bruins named former player [Don Sweeney](/wiki/Don_Sweeney "Don Sweeney") as the team's new general manager for the [2015–16 season](/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_NHL_season "2015–16 NHL season").[[189]](#cite_note-Sweeney-189) Part of Sweeney's offseason moves included trading [Milan Lucic](/wiki/Milan_Lucic "Milan Lucic") to the [Los Angeles Kings](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Kings "Los Angeles Kings") in exchange for goalie [Martin Jones](/wiki/Martin_Jones_(ice_hockey) "Martin Jones (ice hockey)"), forward [Colin Miller](/wiki/Colin_Miller_(ice_hockey,_born_1992) "Colin Miller (ice hockey, born 1992)"), and a 2015 first round draft pick.[[190]](#cite_note-190) The Bruins would flip Jones to the [San Jose Sharks](/wiki/San_Jose_Sharks "San Jose Sharks") four days later for [Sean Kuraly](/wiki/Sean_Kuraly "Sean Kuraly") and a 2016 first round pick.[[191]](#cite_note-191) The Bruins played in the [2016 NHL Winter Classic](/wiki/2016_NHL_Winter_Classic "2016 NHL Winter Classic") against the Canadiens, but lost 5–1.[[192]](#cite_note-192) One all-time franchise achievement the Bruins attained in the 2015–16 season is shared by only their greatest rival, the Canadiens – a total of 3,000 wins in the team's existence, achieved by the Bruins on January 8, 2016, in a 4–1 road victory against the New Jersey Devils.[[193]](#cite_note-193) For the first time since the two seasons following the 2004–05 lockout, the Bruins did not qualify for the playoffs in two consecutive seasons.[[194]](#cite_note-194)

fanoutqa_003388.t: War of the Third Coalition :: Periodisation :: chunk_0004
fanoutqa_003388.x:
War of the Third Coalition :: Periodisation :: chunk_0004
Historians differ on when the War of the Third Coalition began and when it ended . From the British perspective , the war started when Britain declared war on France on 18 May 1803, but it was still on its own. It was not until December 1804 when Sweden entered into an alliance with the United Kingdom, not until 11 April 1805 when Russia joined the alliance, not until 16 July when Britain and Russia ratified their treaty of alliance, and only thereafter Austria (9 August) and Naples–Sicily (11 September) completed the fully-fledged coalition.

Meanwhile, [Bavaria](/wiki/Electorate_of_Bavaria "Electorate of Bavaria") sided with France on 25 August following the [Treaty of Bogenhausen](/wiki/Treaty_of_Bogenhausen "Treaty of Bogenhausen"), and [Württemberg](/wiki/Electorate_of_W%C3%BCrttemberg "Electorate of Württemberg") joined Napoleon on 5 September. No major hostilities between France and any member of the coalition other than Britain ([Trafalgar campaign](/wiki/Trafalgar_campaign "Trafalgar campaign") March–November 1805) occurred until the [Ulm Campaign](/wiki/Ulm_Campaign "Ulm Campaign") (25 September – 20 October 1805). This was in part because [Napoleon's planned invasion of the United Kingdom](/wiki/Napoleon%27s_planned_invasion_of_the_United_Kingdom "Napoleon's planned invasion of the United Kingdom") was not called off until 27 August 1805, when he decided to use his invasion force [camped at Boulogne](/wiki/Camp_of_Boulogne "Camp of Boulogne") against Austria instead.

Likewise, no major battles occurred after the Battle of Austerlitz and the signing of the [Peace of Pressburg](/wiki/Peace_of_Pressburg_(1805) "Peace of Pressburg (1805)") on 26 December 1805, which forced Austria to leave the Third Coalition and cease hostilities against France. Some historians conclude that Austria's departure "shattered the fragile Third Coalition" and "ended the War of the Third Coalition".[[1]](#cite_note-FOOTNOT

Lifetime tenure of justices can only be found for US federal judges and the State of Rhode Island's Supreme Court justices, with all other democratic nations and all other US states having set term limits or mandatory retirement ages.[[102]](#cite_note-102) [Larry Sabato](/wiki/Larry_Sabato "Larry Sabato") wrote: "The insularity of lifetime tenure, combined with the appointments of relatively young attorneys who give long service on the bench, produces senior judges representing the views of past generations better than views of the current day."[[103]](#cite_note-tws23oct16-103) [Sanford Levinson](/wiki/Sanford_Levinson "Sanford Levinson") has been critical of justices who stayed in office despite medical deterioration based on longevity.[[104]](#cite_note-tws10oct12-104) [James MacGregor Burns](/wiki/James_MacGregor_Burns "James MacGregor Burns") stated lifelong tenure has "produced a critical time lag, with the Supreme Court institutionally almost always behind the times".[[105]](#cite_note-tws27oct304-105) Proposals to solve these problems include [term limits](/wiki/Term_limit "Term limit") for justices, as proposed by Levinson[[106]](#cite_note-tws10octxx-106) and Sabato[[103]](#cite_note-tws23oct16-103)[[107]](#cite_note-107) and a mandatory retirement age proposed by [Richard Epstein](/wiki/Richard_Allen_Epstein "Richard Allen Epstein"),[[108]](#cite_note-108) among others.[[109]](#cite_note-109) [Alexander Hamilton](/wiki/Alexander_Hamilton "Alexander Hamilton") in *[Federalist 78](/wiki/Federalist_78 "Federalist 78")* argued that one benefit of lifetime tenure was that, "nothing can contribute so much to its firmness and independence as permanency in office".[[110]](#cite_note-tws28oct707-110)

During the year, 5 of the 20 most destructive wildfires in the state's history burned between October and December: #1 Tubbs, #6 Nuns, #7 Thomas, #11 Atlas, and #17 Redwood Valley.[[11]](#cite_note-top_20_most_destructive-11) The wildfires collectively caused at least $18.0 billion (2018 USD) in damages, including $13.2 billion in insured losses, $3 billion in other economic losses, and $1.8 billion in fire suppression costs, making the 2017 California fires the second-costliest on record.[[3]](#cite_note-13.2_billion-3)[[4]](#cite_note-spent-4) The total economic cost, including fire suppression, insurance, direct and indirect economic losses, and recovery expenditures is estimated at $180 billion (2017 USD).[[18]](#cite_note-180_billion-18) This number includes economic harm to the wine industry, where several wineries in Napa and Sonoma were destroyed, and where many wine grapes were severely damaged by smoke. Cal Fire spent $700 million during fiscal year 2017, far exceeding the approximately $426 million the agency had budgeted that year for fire suppression.[[12]](#cite_note-California-12) This made 2017 the most expensive firefighting year on record in California state history.[[19]](#cite_note-new_record-19)

According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, 2017 will be remembered as a year of extremes. It was the third-warmest year on record for the United States, and it was the second-hottest in California, bringing to the surface the question of long-term [climate change](/wiki/Climate_change_in_California "Climate change in California") and its contribution to the 2017 California fires. Grand Theft Auto V :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
Shared between many of Rockstar's studios worldwide, [the game's development](/wiki/Development_of_Grand_Theft_Auto_V "Development of Grand Theft Auto V") began around the time of *Grand Theft Auto IV*'s release. The developers drew influence from many of their previous projects (such as *[Red Dead Redemption](/wiki/Red_Dead_Redemption "Red Dead Redemption")* and *[Max Payne 3](/wiki/Max_Payne_3 "Max Payne 3")*) and designed the game around three lead protagonists to innovate on the core structure of its predecessors. Much of the development work constituted the open world's creation, and several team members conducted field research around California to capture footage for the design team. [The game's soundtrack](/wiki/Music_of_Grand_Theft_Auto_V "Music of Grand Theft Auto V") features an original score composed by a team of producers who collaborated over several years. *Grand Theft Auto V* was released in September 2013 for the [PlayStation 3](/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3") and [Xbox 360](/wiki/Xbox_360 "Xbox 360"), in November 2014 for the [PlayStation 4](/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4") and [Xbox One](/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One"), in April 2015 for [Windows](/wiki/Windows "Windows"), and in March 2022 for the [PlayStation 5](/wiki/PlayStation_5 "PlayStation 5") and [Xbox Series X/S](/wiki/Xbox_Series_X/S "Xbox Series X/S").

Extensively marketed and widely anticipated, the game broke industry sales records and became the fastest-selling entertainment product in history, earning $800 million in its first day and $1 billion in its first three days. It received critical acclaim, with praise directed at its multiple-protagonist design, open world, presentation and gameplay. However, its depiction of violence and women caused controversies. The film's development began when Marvel Studios received a loan from [Merrill Lynch](/wiki/Merrill_Lynch "Merrill Lynch") in April 2005. After the success of the film *[Iron Man](/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film) "Iron Man (2008 film)")* in May 2008, Marvel announced that *The Avengers* would be released in July 2011 and would bring together Stark (Downey), Rogers (Evans), Thor (Hemsworth), and Banner (portrayed by [Edward Norton](/wiki/Edward_Norton "Edward Norton") in the 2008 film *[The Incredible Hulk](/wiki/The_Incredible_Hulk_(film) "The Incredible Hulk (film)")*) from Marvel's previous films. After the signing of Johansson as Romanoff in March 2009, Renner as Barton in June 2010, and Ruffalo to replace Norton as Banner in July 2010, the film was pushed back for a 2012 release. Whedon was hired in April 2010 and rewrote the original screenplay by [Zak Penn](/wiki/Zak_Penn "Zak Penn"). Production began in April 2011 in [Albuquerque, New Mexico](/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico"), before moving to [Cleveland, Ohio](/wiki/Cleveland,_Ohio "Cleveland, Ohio"), in August and New York City in September. The film has more than 2,200 visual effects shots.

*The Avengers* premiered at the [El Capitan Theatre](/wiki/El_Capitan_Theatre "El Capitan Theatre") in Los Angeles on April 11, 2012, and was released in the United States on May 4, as the final film in [Phase One](/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe:_Phase_One "Marvel Cinematic Universe: Phase One") of the MCU. The film received praise for Whedon's direction and screenplay, visual effects, action sequences, acting, and musical score. It grossed over $1.5 billion worldwide, setting numerous box office records and becoming the [third-highest-grossing film of all time](/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films "List of highest-grossing films") at the time of its release and the [highest-grossing film of 2012](/wiki/2012_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2012 in film

**Chad Meredith Hurley** (born January 24, 1977) is an American webmaster and businessman who served as the chief executive officer (CEO) of [YouTube](/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") from its founding until 2010, when he became an advisor to the company. He also co-founded [MixBit](/wiki/MixBit "MixBit"), a since closed video sharing service.[[1]](#cite_note-PC_Magazine-1) In October 2006, he and [Steve Chen](/wiki/Steve_Chen "Steve Chen") sold YouTube for $1.65 billion to [Google](/wiki/Google "Google").[[2]](#cite_note-2) Hurley worked in [eBay](/wiki/EBay "EBay")'s [PayPal](/wiki/PayPal "PayPal") division, where one of his tasks involved designing the original PayPal logo,[[3]](#cite_note-3) before co-founding YouTube[[4]](#cite_note-4) with fellow [PayPal](/wiki/PayPal "PayPal") employees [Steve Chen](/wiki/Steve_Chen "Steve Chen") and [Jawed Karim](/wiki/Jawed_Karim "Jawed Karim").[[5]](#cite_note-usatoday-5) Hurley was primarily responsible for the [tagging](/wiki/Tag_(metadata) "Tag (metadata)") and video-sharing aspects of YouTube.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

After his wife's death, McNamara dated [Katharine Graham](/wiki/Katharine_Graham "Katharine Graham"), with whom he had been friends since the early 1960s. Graham died in 2001.

In September 2004, McNamara wed Diana Masieri Byfield, an Italian-born widow who had lived in the United States for more than 40 years. It was her second marriage. She was married to [Ernest Byfield](/wiki/Ernest_Byfield "Ernest Byfield"), a former [OSS](/wiki/Office_of_Strategic_Services "Office of Strategic Services") officer and Chicago hotel owner, thirty years her senior, whose first wife, Gladys Rosenthal Tartiere, leased her 400-acre (1.6 km2) Glen Ora estate in [Middleburg, Virginia](/wiki/Middleburg,_Virginia "Middleburg, Virginia"), to John F. Kennedy during his presidency.[[74]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoberts2004-78)[[75]](#cite_note-79)

At the end of his life, McNamara was a life trustee on the Board of Trustees of the [California Institute of Technology](/wiki/California_Institute_of_Technology "California Institute of Technology") (Caltech), a trustee of the Economists for Peace and Security, a trustee of the [American University of Nigeria](/wiki/American_University_of_Nigeria "American University of Nigeria"), and an honorary trustee for the [Brookings Institution](/wiki/Brookings_Institution "Brookings Institution").

McNamara died at his home in Washington, D.C., at 5:30 am on 6 July 2009, at the age of 93.[[76]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPage2009-80)[[4]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWeiner2009-4) He is buried at the [Arlington National Cemetery](/wiki/Arlington_National_Cemetery "Arlington National Cemetery") in [Arlington County, Virginia](/wiki/Arlington_County,_Virginia "Arlington County, Virginia"), with the grave marker also commemorating his wives.[[77]](#cite_note-81)

Mirroring their mostly sub-replacement fertility and high [life expectancy](/wiki/Life_expectancy "Life expectancy"), European countries tend to have older populations overall. They had nine of the top ten highest median ages in national populations in 2005. Only [Japan](/wiki/Japan "Japan") had an older population.[[19]](#cite_note-age-19)

None of the cities where we play our championship is named New York, Boston, Los Angeles, Chicago or Miami. We don't play on a campus. We play in professional football arenas.[[51]](#cite_note-Katz_2012-09-07-85)

Under then-current criteria, only eleven stadiums could be considered as Final Four locations.[[51]](#cite_note-Katz_2012-09-07-85) On June 12, 2013, Katz reported that the NCAA had changed its policy. In July 2013, the NCAA had a portal available on its website for venues to make Final Four proposals in the 2017–2020 period, and there were no restrictions on proposals based on venue size. Also, the NCAA decided that future regionals will no longer be held in domes. In Katz's report, Lewis indicated that the use of domes for regionals was intended as a dry run for future Final Four venues, but this particular policy was no longer necessary because all of the Final Four sites from 2014 to 2016 had already hosted regionals.[[52]](#cite_note-Katz_2013-06-12-86) The policy was changed to only be used if a new venue would be hosting the subsequent tournament's Final Four.[[53]](#cite_note-87)[[54]](#cite_note-88) Under the current policy, the 2030 regionals could be held at [Mercedes-Benz Stadium](/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Stadium "Mercedes-Benz Stadium") in Atlanta, which opened in 2017, as it will be hosting its first Final Four in 2031 after its planned 2020 hosting was cancelled.
